exclusion_detail: The abstract names two final compounds, (S)-5b (SCO-792, named first and the one carried into the conclusion) and 6b; the lead was taken as (S)-5b. Its route (Scheme 7: ester hydrolysis then amide coupling to give 19, acylation with 4-carbamimidamidobenzoyl chloride, hydrogenolysis) starts from the optically active dihydrobenzofuran ester (S)-17b, which has no preparation in this paper and is only cited to a patent ('Production method of optically active dihydrobenzofuran derivatives', WO 2012111849), i.e. prepared as previously reported. The alternative lead 6b is not shorter (cycloaddition/hydrolysis, di-tert-butyl esterification, hydrogenolysis, chiral resolution, acylation, TFA deprotection, desalting: 6 or more steps plus a prepared aldoxime 21).

lead.label: (S)-5b (SCO-792)
lead.why: Abstract: 'revealed two series of potent enteropeptidase inhibitors, a dihydrobenzofuran analogue ((S)-5b, SCO-792) and phenylisoxazoline (6b)'; conclusion: 'identification of (S)-5b (SCO-792) as a potent enteropeptidase inhibitor'. Two compounds are named in the abstract; (S)-5b is first.

notes: 1c (7a = 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid, 5.00 g = 32.9 mmol, so MW 152; glycine tBu ester amide 8a, acylation, deprotection) and 2a (7a + di-tert-butyl L-aspartate -> 15a? / 9b -> 2a) look like 3-step routes from commercial 7a, but I did not verify each procedure in full. The (S)-5b SMILES stereocentre assignment was not checked against a drawn structure (only the printed name was used). No SI file in the bundle.
